simple.meaning: פָּלִיל (pâlîyl) is a Hebrew word meaning “a magistrate.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פָּלִיל (H6414) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 21:22, with occurrences in Exodus, Deuteronomy, Job.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּלִיל (H6414) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פָּלִיל (H6414) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פָּלִיל (pâlîyl) / H6414 is traced through Exodus 21:22, Deuteronomy 32:31, Job 31:11 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6414. palil [ מָּלִיל ] noun masculine judge ; plural מְּלִילִים Deut 32:31 our enemies being judges, umpires ; פ ׳עָוֺן Job 31:11 , read פ ׳עֲוֺן according to Di Siegf, compare De; < מְּלִילִי עָוֺן as 31:28 , so Bu Du; בִּפְלִלִים Exod 21:22 , read perhaps בַּנְּפָלִים for the abortion Bu ZAW xi (1891), 107 , compare also Di-Ry.

occurrences.englishText: “If men fight and hurt a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely, and yet no harm follows, he shall be surely fined as much as the woman’s husband demands and the judges allow.
For their rock is not as our Rock,
For that would be a heinous crime.
